extracted.intended_audience: citizen petitioners under TSCA Section 21 (e.g., Tribes, NGOs), and EPA staff involved in petition review and TSCA Section 6 rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements the EPA applies when reviewing a TSCA Section 21 citizen petition requesting initiation of a TSCA Section 6(a) rulemaking (including evidentiary, science, and procedural expectations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition content requirement (TSCA Section 21(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: TSCA Section 21(b)(1) requires that the petition “set forth the facts which it is claimed establish that it is necessary” to initiate the proceeding requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Burden is on the petitioners to present the facts establishing necessity. During the 90-day petition review period, EPA may in its discretion also consider relevant information reasonably available to the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of 'necessary' incorporates TSCA Section 6 standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition must establish it is “necessary” to initiate a TSCA Section 6 rulemaking; that “necessary” language implicitly incorporates the statutory standards that apply to the requested actions under TSCA Section 6(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The relevant standard is found in TSCA Section 6(a), which requires the Administrator to formally “determine” there is an unreasonable risk before issuing a rule under section 6. Thus petitions should be framed to demonstrate facts supporting initiation of a proceeding consistent with Section 6 standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-evaluation substantive criteria (hazard, exposure, best available science, weight-of-evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the risk evaluation is to determine whether a chemical substance presents an unreasonable risk of injury to health or the environment, under the conditions of use, including an unreasonable risk to a relevant potentially exposed or susceptible subpopulation identified as relevant by the Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of the risk evaluation EPA must evaluate both hazard and exposure; exclude consideration of costs or other non-risk factors; use scientific information and approaches consistent with the best available science; and ensure decisions are based on the weight-of-scientific-evidence (15 U.S.C. 2605(b)(4)(F); 15 U.S.C. 2625(h) and (i)). TSCA Section 26(h)-(i) and 26(k) further require using best available science, considering relevance and uncertainties, and considering information reasonably available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitioner need only show unreasonable risk for one or more conditions of use
rubrics_metrics.description: A TSCA Section 21 citizen petitioner need only present facts demonstrating that a chemical substance poses an unreasonable risk due to one or more conditions of use, not all conditions of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited case law: Food & Water Watch, Inc. v. EPA. Petitioners do not have to demonstrate unreasonable risk across every possible use to warrant initiation of a proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: EPA may consider all reasonably available information during review
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the burden of factual presentation is on petitioners, EPA in its discretion may consider relevant information that is reasonably available to the agency during the 90-day petition review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA exercised this discretion in the 6PPD petition by considering petition materials together with reasonably available data, literature searches, ECOTOX curation, and agency-generated analyses to evaluate necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of alternatives when proposing prohibitions or bans (TSCA Section 6(c)(2)(C))
rubrics_metrics.description: When deciding whether to prohibit or ban a use, TSCA Section 6(c)(2)(C) requires EPA to “consider, to the extent practicable, whether technically and economically feasible alternatives that benefit health or the environment ... will be reasonably available as a substitute when the proposed prohibition or other restriction takes effect.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions requesting bans should provide or consider information on feasible alternatives; EPA will coordinate with other programs and states (e.g., California Safer Consumer Products, Washington Safer Products for Washington) to inform alternatives assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of remedial rulemaking under TSCA Section 6(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: If EPA determines the manufacture, processing, distribution in commerce, use, or disposal of a chemical presents an unreasonable risk, EPA conducts a rulemaking to apply one or more TSCA Section 6(a) requirements to the extent necessary so that the chemical no longer presents such risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In proposing and promulgating rules under Section 6(a), EPA considers provisions of TSCA Sections 6(c)(2), 6(d), 6(g), and 9. EPA retains discretion over the content and timing of any regulation and is not required to adopt the exact measures requested by petitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of TSCA authorities to obtain additional information (Sections 8(d) and 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA may use other TSCA authorities to collect data needed to understand and characterize risk (e.g., pursue a rulemaking under TSCA Section 8(d) to require manufacturers to submit lists and copies of unpublished health and safety studies, and require development of new information under TSCA Section 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA intends to finalize an 8(d) rule (requiring reporting of unpublished studies) before 2025 with reporting 90 days after publication; information collected may inform subsequent requirements (rules, orders, consent agreements) under Section 4 or other authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence needed to link source to exposures and reduce uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: To increase certainty associated with exposure data, evidence showing that 6PPD in tires is the primary source for 6PPD-quinone in stormwater and surface water is beneficial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA would need data on other product sources of 6PPD (e.g., footwear, synthetic turf, playgrounds), relative volumes/masses used in each product type, and additional fate-and-transport research on tire wear particles; monitoring and exposure data quality evaluation are important (e.g., measured exceedances of LC50 for sensitive species).

rubrics_metrics.name: Science-quality and coordination expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions under TSCA Sections 4, 5, and 6 must use scientific information, technical procedures, measures, methods, protocols, methodologies, or models employed in a manner consistent with the best available science and be based on the weight of scientific evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA will coordinate across offices (ORD, OW, Regions), with federal partners, Tribes, states, industry, and academia, and leverage literature searches, ECOTOX database curation, development of screening values, monitoring methods, ecotoxicity studies, fate/transport research, and other targeted research to meet these scientific standards.
